topic: Neural Network Learning: The Intuition of Backpropagation
target_audience: University students with basic knowledge of functions and calculus

sections.title: The Analogy: Learning through Trial and Error
lecture_lines: Neural networks are machines that learn from mistakes.
Imagine a student shooting a basketball at a hoop.
The distance from the hoop is the error.
animations: Flash incorrect guess (red circle) near answer. (#FF0000)
Fade in feedback arrow correcting the guess. (#00FF00)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Loss Landscape
lecture_lines: Error values form a complex topographical landscape.
We aim to find the lowest valley here.
Each weight acts like a coordinate on this map.
animations: Animate a 2D topographical loss function curve. (#FFFFFF)
Flash a 'deep valley' at the curve's global minimum. (#FFFF00)
Move a ball (the weight state) along the curve. (#00FFFF)

sections.title: The Forward Pass: Making a Guess
lecture_lines: Data moves forward through the network layers.
Matrix operations and functions process this input data.
The result is a final prediction score.
animations: Display layers of nodes connected by thin lines. (#FFFFFF)
Animate data packets traveling forward across connections. (#00FF00)
Pop up the final prediction score at output. (#FFFF00)

sections.title: The Heart of the Lesson: Backpropagation Intuition
lecture_lines: Backpropagation is like assigning blame for mistakes.
We start at the output error point.
The chain rule moves blame backward through layers.
Each weight receives its contribution to the error.
This blame helps us adjust individual weights precisely.
animations: Show the output error as a large red node. (#FF0000)
Animate pulses of 'blame' moving backward through connections. (#FF9900)
Change color of each connection based on blame intensity. (#00FFFF)
Resize nodes as they adjust to new blame values. (#FFCC00)
Show final stabilized state of the neural network. (#FFFFFF)

sections.title: Updating Weights: Gradient Descent
lecture_lines: We adjust weights to decrease the total error.
This process is known as gradient descent.
Repeating this loop refines the neural network's performance.
animations: Draw loss function graph with current weight marker. (#FFFFFF)
Show weight marker sliding down toward lower loss. (#FFFF00)
Pulse the weight marker when reaching the minimum. (#00FF00)
